newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot natgas surges with futures, swing demand.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot natgas surges with futures, swing demand.

text.p: U.S. spot natgas prices were sharply higher early Wednesday, but buyers backed away shortly before nomination deadlines, thereby deflating the rally, industry sources said.

Louisiana Gulf Coast prices at the Henry Hub soared to a high of $2.25 but eased late to a low of $2.17 per mmBtu. Transco was quoted in the mid-to-high $2.20s. On average, prices were up 12 cents on the day.
Traders blamed the sharp price uptick on end-of-the-month balancing needs, storage injection demand and lingering air-conditioning demand in the Southwest.
At 1409 EDT, May Henry Hub natgas futures were 3.4 cents higher at $2.148 after hitting a high of $2.20 early in the session.

The rise in Gulf prices was passed onto the Northeast market areas. At the New York city-gate, prices were quoted at least 15 cents higher at $2.43-2.55, while Appalachian values were at $2.37-2.46 on Columbia and about $2.50 on CNG.
Similarly at the Chicago city-gate, values jumped early to a high of $2.39, up about 20 cents from Tuesday. Late morning deals were reported done at $2.29-2.31.
Elsewhere in the Midcontinent, prices on average gained 10 cents to $2.00-2.08, with Demarcation quoted mostly at $2.04-2.07.

Further west, Permian basin prices once again showed the sharpest move, surging 15 cents to an average of $2.09-2.10. Deals were reported done anywhere from $2 to $2.15, with the higher-priced gas evident in early trading.
Waha values were similarly higher at $2.13-2.18, while southern California border prices gained eight cents to $2.10-2.20.
Above-normal temperatures in the western part of the Southwest continued to drain supplies in that region, but cooler weather was forecast to arrive later this week.
Contributing to the tight supply were storage plays.
"Storage players took profits based on first-of-the-month prices," one market source said, referring to the late morning drop in prices.
In south Texas, prices rose 12 cents to about $2.15. Slightly below-normal temperatures were forecast to continue in the state over the next few days, Weather Services Corp said.

Expectations for today's American Gas Association storage report have ranged anywhere from a draw of 30 bcf to an injection of 30 bcf, with most traders anticipating a modest build. A year ago stocks rose 27 bcf.
